root_cause.text: The `plic_irq_eoi` function incorrectly relied on the generic IRQ descriptor's disabled flag (`irqd_irq_disabled`) to verify interrupt enablement, failing to detect when the PLIC hardware's per-hart enable bit was cleared during affinity changes while the interrupt was active.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the `irqd_irq_disabled(d)` check with a direct read of the PLIC enable register (`readl(reg) & BIT(d->hwirq % 32)`), addressing the issue described where "the enable bit for the handling hart can be zero despite irqd_irq_disabled(d) being false."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes PLIC EOI handler to check actual hardware interrupt enable state rather than IRQ descriptor state before toggling interrupt
intent_record.what: Added two local variables (reg and enabled) to read the hardware enable register for the IRQ, changed the condition from checking irqd_irq_disabled(d) to checking !enabled by reading the actual hardware enable bit
intent_record.how: Changes the EOI path to verify the actual hardware interrupt enable state instead of relying on the IRQ descriptor's software state, ensuring plic_toggle is only called when the hardware enable bit is not set
